success_patterns: For collection and search requests without an explicit page, the initial page and documented default search settings may still be needed: Wayfair search and review calls repeatedly use page 1, and Wayfair search also uses its conventional page size and documented default sort.

patch.reasoning: The skill covers pagination when the user explicitly requests a page, but not the common initial retrieval when no page is stated. Multiple trajectories show that omitting initial-page and standard search settings can leave otherwise-correct calls incomplete.

edits.target: When the user explicitly requests the first page, pass `page=1` on every applicable paginated call; do the same where applicable when a requested count is served by a paginated endpoint.
edits.content: Treat a request to retrieve a collection or perform a search as an initial-page request when no page is specified: pass the documented first-page value (usually `1`) to applicable paginated endpoints, even if the user did not explicitly say “first page.” When a page-size parameter is exposed, use the smallest conventional size needed unless the user requests a count or the endpoint documents another default. For initial list or search calls, use a documented default-sort value when the endpoint convention calls for it; do not guess. Apply the same first-page value when the user explicitly requests the first page or a requested count is served by a paginated endpoint.
